comment: Pull requests GitHub reports as MERGED whose merge commit is not reachable
from `main`, and which tools/check_merged_prs_landed.py therefore reports
as KNOWN rather than as a finding. Issue #1342.
Every entry was merged into a base branch other than `main`. Two things
produce that: a base branch that had already been squash-merged, which
strands the work; and a stacked PR whose parent branch was later squashed
to main, which carries the work under a different commit. The checker
cannot tell those apart from ancestry alone - a squash breaks the link in
both cases - so each note below records what was MEASURED on main, and
says so when the claim is second-hand instead.
This ratchet SHRINKS ONLY. An entry whose merge commit becomes reachable
from main has been merged properly after all, and the checker FAILS until
the entry is deleted. An entry may never be added to turn a red check
green: a new stranding is a defect to fix.

unreachable.1236: stacked on agent/146-lower-component-methods. CARRIED: tools/tier_guarantees.py and tests/test_tier_guarantee_matrix.py, both added by this merge, are on main.
unreachable.1296: merged into agent/1196-ui-transaction-phases, already squashed to main. Work reported carried by PR #1325 (issue #1342); not independently verified here - it added no files, so there is no cheap witness.
unreachable.1305: merged into agent/1198-private-peer-pool. CARRIED: src/revl/pool_receipt.py, docs/design/566-pool-execution-receipts.md and tests/test_pool_receipts_524.py, all added by this merge, reached main under commit 32db56d9 (PR #1363, the same title). Measured on 773c6e3f6: all three are BYTE-IDENTICAL to this merge's copies, and tests/test_pool_receipts_524.py collects and passes, 17 tests. The note said STRANDED until then; that claim is retired, not still open.
unreachable.1308: merged into agent/81-stream-tiers. REWORKED: `document_holds_stream`, added by this merge to selfhost/emit_go.rvl, is still absent from main and is deliberately not restored. Reading `subscribe` / `stream-iter` there would move those discriminants out of the go tier's `unported` baseline in tests/fixtures/selfhost_blind_spots.json on the strength of a refusal predicate. Main reaches the same outcome by the cheaper route issue #1321 took: the marker's suppression now also requires that no component be OBSERVABLE, and `component_is_observable` reads the LENGTH of a component's `body`, so a stream component is named without any stream spelling being read. Measured on 773c6e3f6 with this merge's two single-arm cases re-authored against that rule: a source-only `Stream.source()` acquisition and a subscription with no loop are both named, one marker per components entry, each holding the reference to emitting `stc-go` where the port emits its marker. Those two cases are on main in tests/test_selfhost_emit_go.py.
